title: Maximum Chunks to Sort

concept.title: A stack of chunk maxima
body: Cut the array into consecutive chunks, sort each chunk on its own, and put the chunks back. The result is sorted exactly when **every element of a chunk is at most every element of the chunks after it**. You want as many chunks as possible.

Process the elements left to right and keep a stack with one number for every chunk: its **maximum**. A new element `x` starts a new chunk. But if `x` is smaller than the maximum of the chunk(s) before it, it must belong to them, so they merge into one chunk whose maximum is the largest of the merged maxima.

body.code:
stack = []
for x in a:
    mx = x
    while stack and stack[-1] > x:     # the previous chunk has a bigger element than x
        mx = max(mx, stack.pop())      # merge it
    stack.append(mx)
answer = len(stack)

body: The stack keeps the chunk maxima in increasing order. Every element is pushed once and popped at most once, so the algorithm is O(n).

statement: Split an array of `n` integers (duplicates are possible) into the largest possible number of consecutive chunks such that sorting every chunk separately and joining them gives the whole array sorted in non-decreasing order. Print the number of chunks.
outputFormat: Print the largest number of chunks.
hints: Maintain a stack with the maximum of every chunk found so far.
A new element smaller than the top maximum must merge into that chunk (and maybe the ones below it).
The number of chunks is the size of the stack at the end.

explanation: The stack holds one maximum per chunk, in increasing order. A smaller new element merges the chunks whose maximum exceeds it. The final stack size is the number of chunks.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

stack = []
for x in a:
    mx = x
    while stack and stack[-1] > x:
        mx = max(mx, stack.pop())
    stack.append(mx)
print(len(stack))
